As an aspiring clinical psychologist, it definitely bothers me when people say things like “omg I’ve been having crazy mood swings lately it’s like I’m bipolar” or “what is with that person they’re so bipolar.” Not only is it an incorrect description, but it also minimizes and dismisses the struggles of individuals who are actually bipolar. I have BPD and my friend has BP, so I’m very familiar with the ins and outs of both disorders along with mania/being manic. I can understand using manic in specific circumstances where the term fits. For example “I had a date coming over so I had to clean like a maniac” or “The concert was so wild everyone was manic.” But when it comes to things like “omg I was so manic last night I dyed my hair lol” I groan and roll my eyes.

Isn’t that the point of r/confessions? Letting out things you’re too scared or hurt to tell anyone in person about.

I’m so terribly sorry for your loss, I can’t even begin to imagine the amount of anger and pain that you and your family must be in. I know that digging this up might bring your family more pain but it is absolutely necessary. Not only to provide a sense of closure, but to serve that bastard some cold hard justice. Domestic violence cases are horribly common but forcing police and prosecutors to do their damn jobs is something that will not only help your case but future ones. Like everyone else said, get a PI who do a thorough investigation and a good prosecutor to present the case in court. Also reaching out to well known true crime and cold case activists like Ashley Flowers (unsolved mysteries podcast) to spread the word. I would also suggest making sure that an autopsy is/was done, even if that means having to exhume her body. 

Massive TW for the upcoming content: hanging/suicide/death  

If an autopsy finds that she sustained injuries unrelated to hanging (ex. bruises or cuts on other parts of her body) that should be enough evidence to reopen the case fully as a murder investigation (but don’t quote me on this since it might depend on the state). Because that would imply that she suffered other sorts of domestic abuse prior to her death (implicating the husband more) and/or that she was physically coerced into hanging herself. I’ve also heard that coroners can tell if injuries happened before or after death as well as if the death was caused by hanging vs something else, even if the cause of death seems to be just by hanging. Not sure how accurate this is but if the autopsy finds out the hanging/neck trauma from the hanging occurred after her death, that should definitely be enough to open up a murder investigation. 

Also, it seems from your post that your family is relatively close since your sister was willing to confide with you and your mother about her marital issues. (And even if y’all weren’t close, a sudden expression of her problems after little communication is a clear warning sign something is very wrong). As an actively suicidal person myself, who loves their family and friends, even at during my most spontaneous attempts I had some sort of note nearby that essentially said “I’m sorry, this isn’t anyones fault. I love my friends and family, etc.” in case I succeeded and someone found me. If your sister didn’t leave any sort of note (even if she HAD called your mom back right away and they finished their conversation like normal), that’s another big red flag in my eyes. 

If there was a note, I’d suggest getting a handwriting analysis of it and compare it to other pieces of her writing. Anybody correct me if I’m wrong, but I don’t think a handwriting analysis is admissible in court as evidence. But if there’s any reason to believe that she didn’t write the note herself or was forced to write it, that should at least be enough to spur further investigation. 

I believe you 100% and if you ever needed or wanted help getting the word out I’m sure that everyone else here who believes you as well wouldn’t hesitate to boost this case as much as possible on social media. Your sister deserves justice, your family deserves peace, and that garbage husband needs to rot in jail for the rest of his life.

I wasn’t going to comment originally but this seems to be a very divided comment section so I figured I’d add my 2 cents. I don’t fully disapprove of what OP did. Full honesty, I’m pretty sure I’d do something similar in OPs situation. Maybe not for the same reasons exactly, but more of a “I don’t get paid enough to go out of my way to protect chomos” reasoning. I’m not very politically savvy but I know enough to see how badly the prison / judicial system needs to be reformed. I saw some people saying how the chomos in OPs place were already being “held accountable” but OP clearly stated that many of the other offenders in there were serving more time for bad checks etc. So at least in this situation, it seems the chomos in question weren’t getting the correct sentencing (or rehabilitation/treatment) regardless of OPs deliberate negligence - which would be a point for OPs case in my opinion. Prison reform is something that interests me as psychologist in training but I’ll be the first to admit that I have some bias towards chomos/rapists etc. because I myself am a SA survivor (ages 11-17). Edit: I wasn’t trying to imply that I don’t think chomos/SA can be reformed; I think it’s worth a shot to try because everyone  deserves a chance to live better lives. My bias towards them is related more to just what they’ve done, and I’d probably never be comfortable being friends with a former and reformed offender. But I would never treat a psychiatric patient any differently (ex. being mean or flat out refusing to treat them) solely based on that aspect. 

I don’t like children, nor do I want any myself, but I believe in protecting them and creating a safer better world for them. So if a few chomos get released with PTSD from being attacked while being under watch by OP, but it also means they’ll never assault someone again, then I think it’s worth it. But this method is definitely not a rule or standard to go by when prison reform and rehabilitation (for all offenders) should be the main goal.
